activities.title: WWI cause map overview
activities.body: Read the short model and note the three parts. Keep the sequence in mind.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions created rival blocs and rising pressure before 1914.

activities.label: Explain the outbreak path
activities.title: Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Explain the sequence from Sarajevo to declarations of war in your own words. Use the exact order, not just the names.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination began the July Crisis, and the crisis ended with declarations of war spreading the conflict.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names Sarajevo, the July Crisis, and declarations of war in order. If the order is unclear, repair the middle step first.

activities.label: Fix the timeline gap
activities.title: Repair the war timeline
activities.body: Correct the mixed-up part and try again in one sentence. Keep the dates and events in order.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Putting the armistice before U.S. entry or treating 1914, 1917, and 1918 as interchangeable dates.
activities.correctAnswer: 1914 is the outbreak year, 1917 is the year the United States entered the war, and 1918 is the armistice year.
activities.feedback: The fix is to keep 1914, 1917, and 1918 separate and in order. A correct answer names each year with its matching event.

activities.label: Re-explain the full story
activities.title: War story in plain words
activities.body: Explain the whole cause map again from memory. Use one clear chain from tensions to the end date.
activities.correctAnswer: Prewar European alliances and tensions created rival blocs, the Sarajevo assassination led into the July Crisis and declarations of war, and the war ran from 1914 to the 1918 armistice.
activities.feedback: A strong answer connects all three parts in one chain. If one part is missing, add it without changing the order.

activities.label: Check the timeline
activities.title: Choose the right sequence
activities.body: Pick the best sequence from the choices. Answer without notes.
activities.feedback: That sequence matches the basic war chronology. The key is to keep outbreak, U.S. entry, and armistice in the right year order.

activities.title: Return to this map later
activities.body: Write one thing to review later and one part you still want to strengthen.

check.title: Alliance blocs before war
check.prompt: How did prewar European alliances divide the major powers?
check.referenceAnswer: They divided the major powers into the Triple Entente and the Triple Alliance blocs.
check.feedback: The key point is the two opposing alliance blocs, not a single general alliance system.

items.essentialIdea: The Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum, then Serbia, then wider war.

check.title: From assassination to war
check.prompt: What sequence followed the Sarajevo assassination before the war widened?
check.referenceAnswer: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, Serbia responded, and the conflict widened into war.
check.feedback: The sequence matters: assassination first, then ultimatum, then responses and escalation.

items.essentialIdea: 1914 began the war, and 1918 ended it with the armistice.

check.title: War start and end
check.prompt: Which years mark the start and end of World War I?
check.referenceAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.
check.feedback: Use the start and end years together; 1918 is tied to the armistice ending the fighting.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify the war's end year
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which year ended World War I with the armistice?
recognitionCheck.feedback: 1918 is the armistice year that ended the fighting.

session.methodReason: The learner is starting from zero and asked for the big picture first, so establish a connected causal model before asking for independent explanation.
contentTargets: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
completionEvidence: Describe the main alliance blocs and at least three prewar tensions using the example provided
Place Sarajevo, the July Crisis, the start of the war, U.S. entry, and the armistice in order
Label each uncertain idea as a cause, event, or consequence

learnerProfile.commonBlocker: Large amounts of new information feel overwhelming
learnerProfile.guidancePreference: Show one visible step at a time
learnerProfile.explanationPreference: Give the big picture before the details and one concrete example first
learnerProfile.startingPattern: Starts more consistently when the first action is small and specific
learnerProfile.primaryImprovementGoal: Understand the story first, then remember the details
learnerProfile.memoryChallenge: I forget some ideas after a few days
learnerProfile.supportPreference: Give a small hint before showing the answer
learnerProfile.freeformContext: I know almost nothing about World War I yet.
